### Observed differences

- In the later window, A04 appears in about 72 in 100 traces, up from about 15 in 100, with mean occurrences per trace rising from 0.16 to 0.79; it also occurs much earlier in the case (mean relative position about 0.17 versus 0.53 before). [OCC001, POS001]
- A04 now typically sits between A14 and A15: about 89 in 100 of A04's outgoing transitions go to A15 (before, its transitions were spread out, the largest share about 17 in 100 to A52); A14 now leads to A04 in about 70 in 100 of its transitions, where before about 83 in 100 went straight to A15; A14 precedes A04 in about 65 in 100 traces (from about 12), A04 precedes A15 in about 40 in 100 traces (from about 2), and the pairs A14→A04 and A04→A15 are now adjacent in about 98 and 50 in 100 of observed cases respectively. [DIR002, DIR005, REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG005]
- A06, A08 and A10 are executed far less often: participation falls to about 7, 6 and 6 in 100 traces respectively, from about 23, 18 and 20. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- The group A19, A20, A25, A26 now runs earlier in the case (mean relative position about 0.60 down to about 0.34) and its order relative to A27/A28 reverses: A19 precedes A27 in about 22 in 100 traces versus 0 before, A25 precedes A27 in about 30 versus under 1, with similar reversals for A20 and A26, whereas previously A27/A28 typically preceded them. [POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019]
- Routing around this group changed accordingly: about 92–97 in 100 of the outgoing transitions of A19, A20, A25 and A26 now go to A27 (before, mostly A33 and A29 at about 40–55 in 100); A46 now leads into the group (its transitions to A27 drop from about 83 in 100 to about 1, while A25/A26/A19/A20 take about 21–29 each, and A46→A26 is adjacent in about 90 in 100 of 48 observed pairs); the former A29→A19 and A29→A26 adjacencies have essentially disappeared. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR013, LAG019, LAG016, LAG017]
- The A28→A29→A33 sequence tightens: A28 goes to A29 in about 97 in 100 of its transitions (from about 49), A29 goes to A33 in about 99 in 100 (from about 47), and A28 reaches A33 mostly at lag 2 instead of lag 3. [DIR011, DIR012, LAG014, LAG015, LAG018]
- Smaller shifts: A15, A27, A28, A29 and A46 sit slightly later (mean relative position up about 0.02–0.05), and A02's outgoing mix changes on few observations (39 transitions before, 20 after). [POS002, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of two structural differences. First, in the later window A04 runs on most cases as an early step between A14 and A15 (A14 → A04 → A15), whereas before, A14 led mostly directly to A15 and A04 was rare; A06, A08 and A10 now appear in only about 6–7 in 100 cases, coinciding with A04's rise. Second, the block A19/A20/A25/A26 now executes before A27/A28 — fed by A46 and followed by the tightened A27→A28→A29→A33 sequence — whereas before it ran after A29. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR002, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR013, REL001, REL002, REL012, REL016, LAG001, LAG005, LAG019]

The support rests on direct relational and routing evidence rather than position shifts alone, and the distinct differences (at least two or three coherent clusters, clearly more than the roughly 0.86 items expected by chance among 172 tested units) are backed by large supports: about 144–158 traces behind the A04 items, 200 in 200 traces behind the order relations, and 47–63 transitions behind the rerouted activities. [OCC001, DIR002, REL012, LAG019]

Limitations: the many items around A04 describe one underlying difference, not independent confirmations, and the A06/A08/A10 decline may be a by-product of the rerouting through A04 rather than a separate change. Some items rest on very few observations — A02's routing change (20 transitions after) and several lag items with only 1–2 observed pairs after the change point — and could be sampling noise. The evidence cannot rule out that differences in the mix of process variants between the two finite samples, rather than a control-flow modification, account for part of these patterns. [DIR001, LAG010, LAG016, LAG017, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
